headline: Acquisition and organic growth drive a sharp profit surge
summary_short: nVent Electric's Q2 FY2026 revenue jumped 52.8% y/y to $1,471.3 million and net income rose 97.2% y/y to $215.9 million, with diluted EPS up 97.0% y/y to $1.32, driven by the Electrical Products Group acquisition and organic infrastructure demand.
summary_long: Q2 FY2026 net sales rose 52.8% y/y to $1,471.3M, driven by ~46 points of organic growth in infrastructure and commercial/residential markets plus $51.6M from the Electrical Products Group acquisition. Gross margin contracted 0.7pt y/y on raw-material/labor inflation, unfavorable mix and capacity investment, partly offset by volume leverage, productivity gains and ~$25M of tariff reimbursements. SG&A fell 4.6pt of sales on organic leverage and restructuring savings despite higher EPG-related amortization. Operating income rose 91.9% y/y to $300.7M; net income grew 97.2% to $215.9M and diluted EPS 97.0% to $1.32, tracking pretax income growth at a flat 22.4% tax rate. Cash rose to $256.0M as $278.7M of operating cash flow outpaced debt repayment, dividends and buybacks. This 10-Q disclosed no forward guidance.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven by roughly 46 points of organic sales gains in infrastructure and commercial/residential end markets plus $51.6 million from the Electrical Products Group acquisition, per the MD&A's own sales bridge.

Dollar profit grew as revenue outpaced costs, but margin fell 0.7pt y/y on raw-material/labor inflation, unfavorable mix and capacity investment, partly offset by volume leverage, productivity gains and ~$25M of tariff reimbursements.
Rose alongside higher sales volume and inflationary raw-material and labor costs; the filing cites the same mix and capacity-investment pressures that compressed gross margin.

SG&A fell 4.6pt of sales on organic-growth leverage and restructuring savings, despite higher EPG-related intangible amortization and inflation, lifting operating income alongside gross profit growth.
Tracks operating income's 91.9% y/y rise; long-term debt fell 15.5% y/y, implying lower interest expense also contributed, though the filing doesn't break out interest expense separately.
Tracks pretax income's growth at an effective tax rate the filing states was flat at 22.4% for both six-month comparison periods.
Tracks net income's 97.2% y/y growth almost exactly, since diluted weighted-average shares rose only 0.3% y/y.
Tracks net income's 97.2% y/y growth; basic share count was essentially flat y/y.

Operating cash flow of $278.7 million in H1 2026 (vs. $154.9 million in H1 2025), driven mainly by higher net income, outpaced $68.3 million of debt repayment, $68.2 million of dividends, $57.6 million of capex and $50.4 million of buybacks.
Declined on $68.3 million of debt repayments in H1 2026 per the cash-flow statement, with no new long-term debt issuance disclosed this year, unlike H1 2025's $275 million issuance.
Not explained in the release — the current portion of long-term debt was unchanged at $13.8 million across all three comparison periods.
Grew mainly from retained-earnings accretion (Q1 and Q2 net income of $142.4M and $215.9M) after dividends declared, per the equity roll-forward statement; no buybacks reduced equity this quarter.
Modest 0.3% y/y increase reflects equity-compensation issuances only partly offset by the $50.4 million of ordinary-share buybacks executed in Q1 2026.

The filing attributes the sharp y/y gains in sales, profit and margin dollars mainly to the Electrical Products Group acquisition and organic infrastructure/data-center demand, partly offset by tariff-related cost inflation; no forward guidance appears in a 10-Q.
